extracted.intended_audience: applicants and agents for design and trade mark registration; Patent Office staff and legal practitioners advising on registrations under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act 1883
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing applications, forms, fees, representations, advertisement, opposition, appeals, and register entries for designs and trade marks under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act, 1883 (UK).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees payable for design registrations and related acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific fees are payable for a range of design office actions (e.g., application to register one design applied to single articles in each class; applications for sets; notice of appeal; copy of certificate; certificate for legal proceedings; notice of intended exhibition; inspection; copy of design; correction of clerical error; request for search; entering new address; office copy per 100 words; certifying office copies), with amounts specified in the First Schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All fees are payable by stamped forms. Note: two kinds of application form for classes 1–12 (10d) and classes 13–14 (1s). The 'set' includes any number of articles ordinarily on sale together irrespective of varieties. See First Schedule for itemised amounts and notes on minimum charges (e.g., office copy never less than 1s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms required for designs (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prescribed set of forms (Form E Application to Register; F Appeal to Board of Trade; G Certificate of Registration; H Application for Copy of Certificate; I Request for Certificate for use in Legal Proceedings; J Certificate for use in Legal Proceedings; K Request to enter Name of Subsequent Proprietor; L Notice of intending Exhibition of Unregistered Design; M Request for Correction or New Address; N Request for Search under Sect. 63; O Application to Register Design for Set of Articles; plus others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two versions of certain forms exist (for classes 1–12 and for classes 13–14) because of differing stamps/fees. Some forms issued with the Instructions are additional to original list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content for registration of a design
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must state the class, name/address/description of the individual or firm claiming to be proprietor, address for return, and a 'Statement of nature of design' (e.g., whether applicable for pattern or shape).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form must be signed by the applicant. One copy of the form is stamped with 10d for classes 1–12 and a second copy with 1s for classes 13–14. See S.47 and Form O for sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Board of Trade (format and accompaniment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal against refusal to register a design must be accompanied by an unstamped copy and a written statement of the case to be submitted to the Board of Trade, written on foolscap paper with a margin of two inches on the left-hand side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules 16–20 for procedure. The form text prescribes the formality of address and submission (to Comptroller, Designs Branch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of registration content
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate certifies that a design copy was registered on a particular day in pursuance of the Act, identifies the class, and states that a copyright of five years is granted for the design's application to the articles in that class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate bears the seal of the Patent Office and the registration number; corresponds to Form G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for copy of certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: A Request for Copy of Certificate form must specify the Certificate of Registration number and class and be dated and signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See s.49 and associated form; submitted to Comptroller, Designs Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for certificate for use in legal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Request must state the use in the suit or the title of the legal proceeding (i.e., the purpose for which the certificate is required) and enclose the entry/thing to be certified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Designs Rules 31; request filed to Comptroller, with form particulars of use to be inserted by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to enter name of subsequent proprietor (declaration requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to enter a subsequent proprietor must include name/address/description of claimant, state how entitlement arose (death, marriage, bankruptcy, assignment, etc.), and include a solemn statutory declaration verifying that the statements comprise every material fact and document affecting proprietorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration made under Statutory Declarations Act 1835, signed before an authority; two kinds of this form are used (stamped differently for classes 1–12 and 13–14). See S.87 and Designs Rules 22–26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intended exhibition of an unregistered design
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must give applicant name and address, state the exhibition (date/place and whether 'opened' or 'is to open'), and insert brief description of design with drawing; to be sent to Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S.57; the notice form indicates enclosure of drawing and the applicable provisions of the Act related to exhibitions. A fee (e.g., 5s indicated on form) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for correction of clerical error or entry of new address
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified form must be used to request correction of clerical errors in the register or to enter a new address; the request is addressed to the Comptroller, Designs Branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S.91 and the form instructions for submission and signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'set' for designs fees and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'set' includes any number of articles ordinarily on sale together irrespective of varieties of size and arrangement in which the design may be shown on each separate article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition affects fee category items for 'set of articles' in the First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of articles of manufacture (designs) — Classes 1–14
rubrics_metrics.description: Third Schedule classifies articles: e.g., Class 1 — articles composed wholly or partly of metal not included in Class 2; Class 2 — jewellery; Class 3 — articles of wood, bone, ivory, papier-mâché, etc.; Class 4 — glass, earthenware, porcelain, bricks, tiles, cement; Class 5 — paper (except hangings); Class 6 — leather incl. bookbinding; Class 7 — paper hangings; Class 8 — carpets and rugs, floorcloths, oil-cloths; Class 9 — lace, hosiery; Class 10 — millinery and wearing apparel incl. boots and shoes; Class 11 — ornamental needlework; Class 12 — goods not included in other classes; Class 13 — printed/woven designs on textiles; Class 14 — handkerchiefs and shawls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification determines appropriate class for registration. If doubt arises as to class of particular goods, the Comptroller determines it (see Trade Marks Rules though this is under Designs Schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade Marks Rules citation and commencement
rubrics_metrics.description: These Rules may be cited as the Trade Marks Rules, 1883, and come into operation immediately after December 31, 1883 (the Act's commencement date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary rule establishing temporal scope; see S.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation tied to Act definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In construing the Rules, words defined by the Act have the meanings assigned by the Act; general definitions are in S.117.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Act for statutory meanings used throughout the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for trade marks actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees to be paid under the Act as it relates to trade marks are those specified in the First Schedule to the Trade Marks Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms for fee transmission referenced in Trade Marks Instructions; amounts and fee categories are set out in First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form for trade mark registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of a trade mark must be made in Form F (Second Schedule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other forms in the Second Schedule may be used where applicable; Form F replaces the Form F in the First Schedule of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goods classification for trade marks and Comptroller's determination
rubrics_metrics.description: For trade mark registration goods are classified as in the Third Schedule; if doubt arises as to which class particular goods belong to, the Comptroller determines the class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By S.65 a trade mark must be registered for particular goods or classes of goods. See note at head of Third Schedule and Instructions for classes 23–25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements on trade mark applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If application is by a firm/partnership it may be signed by one or more members; if by a body corporate it may be signed by the Secretary or principal officer; signature should indicate status (e.g., 'member of firm' or 'for the company').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Form F for example; signature indicates capacity in which signatory acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency for communications with Comptroller
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and all communications may be made by or through an agent duly authorised in writing to the satisfaction of the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications may be by post; agent must be authorised in writing—see Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of application and old marks statement
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt, the Comptroller shall furnish an acknowledgment. If the mark was used before Aug 13, 1876, the application must contain a statement of the time and the person by whom it was so used in respect of the goods in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S.64 Subs. (3) as to 'old trade marks' and further instructions for classes 23–25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size, paper, and margin requirements for documents
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications, notices, counter-statements, representations of marks, and related documents must be upon foolscap paper sized 13 inches by 8 inches, with a left-hand margin of not less than 1.5 inches, and (in some cases) written on one side only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to other directions from the Comptroller; appeals require foolscap with two-inch left margin on one side only. See specific form instructions for margins and single-sided requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification requirement for metal goods in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: In applications for trade marks used on metal goods (other than cutlery, edge tools, and raw steel), the applicant must state in the specification of goods of what metal(s) the goods are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See classes 5 to 14 and Instruction 14 for guidance; this helps class and specification accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number, durability and format of representations of trade marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Three representations of each trade mark (except classes 23–35 where four are required) must be supplied on durable paper of the prescribed size; one representation must be on or affixed to the application form and others on separate half-sheets. Large marks may be pasted and folded onto the sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a drawing/representation cannot be given in this manner, a specimen or copy (full size or reduced) may be sent in the form the Comptroller thinks convenient. The Comptroller may require fresh representations if dissatisfied and may deposit specimens in exceptional cases and refer thereto in the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional journal space fee for large trade marks
rubrics_metrics.description: If a trade mark requires more than 2 inches of the Trade Marks Journal, an additional fee (2d for each additional inch) is payable (First Schedule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects advertisement costs when marks are published in the Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series of trade marks — representation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application relates to a series of trade marks differing in particulars mentioned in S.66, a representation of each trade mark in the series must be made or affixed on the application form and on each separate half-sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See note to S.66 and Instructions; for advertisement the Comptroller may require a statement of how the marks differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of non‑Roman characters
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mark includes words in other than Roman characters, a translation of such words must be given at the foot or on the back of each representation, signed by the applicant or agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates to 'fancy words' marks and ensures intelligibility; See note to S.64 Subs. (C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of sending documents by post
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document authorised or required to be left, made, or given at the Patent Office may be sent by prepaid letter through the post, and if so sent shall be deemed to have been left/made/given when the letter would be delivered in ordinary course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prove service it suffices to prove the letter was properly addressed and put into the post; this Rule implements S.97.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing before the Comptroller when discretionary power exercised
rubrics_metrics.description: Before exercising any discretionary power adversely to the applicant, the Comptroller shall give the applicant ten days' notice of the time when the applicant may be heard personally or by his agent before the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must notify within five days whether he intends to be heard; failure to notify will be communicated on receiving the Comptroller's decision. See S.94.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and time limits for appeal to Board of Trade
rubrics_metrics.description: If Comptroller refuses registration, the applicant intending to appeal must, within one month from the decision date, leave at the Patent Office a notice of intention accompanied by a statement of grounds and a statement of the applicant's case; a copy must be sent to the Secretary of the Board of Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may give directions as to evidence or refer the appeal to the Court. If the Board intends to hear the appeal itself, seven days' notice (or shorter as they direct) of time/place will be given to Comptroller and applicant. See S.62 Subs. (4),(5) and Forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement of application in official paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Every application shall be advertised by the Comptroller in the official paper (The Trade Marks Journal) in such times and manner as the Comptroller may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no representation is inserted in the official paper, the advertisement must refer to where a specimen or representation is deposited for exhibition. The official paper is published weekly and copies are available at Patent Office Library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of advertising — wood block or electrotype requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For advertisement the applicant may be required to furnish a wood block or electrotype (or more) of the trade mark applied to such dimensions as directed by the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Comptroller may require fresh block/electrotype if dissatisfied, and may require different means of advertising if necessary. See Instructions 21–28 for details on blocks/electrotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement of series of marks — additional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is for a series of marks differing as per S.66, the applicant may be required to furnish a wood block or electrotype for each mark in the series; the Comptroller may insert a statement of manner in which the marks differ with the advertisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptroller may direct dimensions and additional advertising measures; costs may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure — mode of bringing matter before Court
rubrics_metrics.description: If a case stands for determination by the Court under S.69, the Comptroller shall require the applicant to issue within one month (or further time allowed) a summons in the chambers for an order to proceed with registration notwithstanding opposition, or to take other proper proceedings for determination by the Court; the applicant must give notice of such proceedings to the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to issue summons or take proceedings within the period (proofed by non-receipt of notice to Comptroller) will be deemed abandonment of the application. Notice to Comptroller must include copy of summons bearing endorsement of service or acceptance of service. Form J for opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of entry on Register of Trade Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as may be after expiration of two months from the date of first advertisement, and subject to any summons or Court determination, if the Comptroller is satisfied the applicant is entitled and the prescribed fee is paid, he shall enter the applicant in the Register as registered proprietor in respect of the goods/classes in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S.78; fees per First Schedule; entries are subject to outstanding proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration where applicant dies before entry
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant dies after application and before entry, the Comptroller, after advertisement period and being satisfied of applicant's death, may enter the person owning the goodwill of the business in place of the deceased applicant if ownership is proved to Comptroller's satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form K is used; this rule is new (per text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries made on registration (date and particulars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon registering a trade mark the Comptroller shall enter in the register the date the application was received (deemed date of registration) and such other particulars as he thinks necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptroller may include additional particulars as needed for registry completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of registration sent to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller shall send notice to the applicant of the registration together with a reference to the advertisement of the trade mark in the official paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 33; constitutes official communication of registration and advertisement reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of proprietor after assignment/transmission (request and declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person entitled to a registered trade mark by assignment, transmission, or operation of law must address a request to the Comptroller, left at the Patent Office, stating name/address/description and particulars of assignment/transmission and showing connection with goodwill; request must be accompanied by a statutory declaration verifying statements and that particulars comprise every material fact/document affecting proprietorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimant must furnish further proof of title and ownership of goodwill as Comptroller may require. In cases of death, will/letters of administration particulars; bankruptcy requires certificate details. Forms: Form E for request, Form K for declaration; Rule 58 governs declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body corporate registration by corporate name
rubrics_metrics.description: A body corporate may be registered as proprietor by its corporate name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard corporate registration practice; see Rule 39.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'applicant' and submission of statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'applicant' includes each of several persons claiming to be registered proprietor of the same trade mark; Comptroller may require any such person to submit a written statement within notified time or attend and make oral explanations as Comptroller requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in Rules 17–19 context regarding hearings and statements; helps Comptroller adjudicate competing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting claims resolution — special case or Court submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Where several persons claim registration of same trade mark and Comptroller refuses registration until rights are determined, the manner of submission to Court shall (unless Court orders otherwise) be by a special case filed and proceeded with like any other special case; the special case may be settled by Comptroller on payment of prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for settling special case (e.g., 2s) set out in First Schedule; Form S for request. Comptroller may settle where parties agree or differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification/variation publication after Court order
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Court orders making/expunging/varying an entry in the register, Comptroller, if he thinks the variation should be public, may publish (by advertisement or otherwise) the circumstances of rectification/variation at the applicant's expense in such manner as he thinks just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of alteration form N; fee payable on rectification (10s per First Schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of trade mark from register and recording cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a trade mark has been removed from the register for nonpayment of prescribed fee or otherwise under S.79, the Comptroller shall enter in the register a record of such removal and the cause thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms for cancellation (Forms O and P) and rules on S.91 apply; preserves register history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration of proprietor's address
rubrics_metrics.description: If registered proprietor sends notice with prescribed fee, the Comptroller shall alter the register accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee payable is 5s (First Schedule); use Form M to notify address change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice before applying to Court to add or alter trade mark
rubrics_metrics.description: When proprietor intends to apply for leave of Court to add to or alter a trade mark under S.92, notice must be given to Comptroller at least 14 days before such application; if leave is granted the applicant must forthwith supply representations of the altered mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptroller will require an adequate number of representations of the altered mark as he deems sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection hours and fees for the Register of Trade Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Register shall be open to public inspection, on payment of prescribed fee, on weekdays between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., except on specified holidays or times notified by placard or when register is required for official use; fee for searching register or classified representations is 1s for every quarter hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include Christmas Day, Good Friday, the day observed as Her Majesty's birthday, bank holidays, days of public fast/thanksgiving, or times posted at the Patent Office. See First Schedule for search fee specifics.
